findings.text: correctness lens, medium: `zbuild_claim_release` never unsets `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED`, so a second invocation is not a no-op as the design requires. (core/claim/claim.sh: "    # Only release if this process acquired the claim     [[ -z "${_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED:-}" ]] && return 0     # Remove zbuild:claimed (advisory; failures never abort the run)     _ccgl_remove_label "$issue" "zbuild:claimed" || true     return 0"; happens when: The design document for this issue states: 'unsets `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED` before calling `_ccgl_remove_label` (advisory). Unsetting first makes a second call a no-op.' Because `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED` is never unset inside the function, any second call that arrives while the variable still holds `"1"` will pass the guard and invoke `_ccgl_remove_label` again on an already-removed label. In production the gh call returns non-zero (label absent), but `|| true` silences it; in the local-fs backend `grep -Fxv` on the already-cleaned file writes an empty replacement and succeeds silently. DSCLA-13 is not affected today because `trap '' TERM` in `_runner_abort_trap` prevents re-entry, but the idempotency guarantee the design chose is absent from the function itself.; fix: code)
